articles.title: Patanjali Foods Q2 profit tanks 19 pc to Rs 420 crore
articles.description: New Delhi, Nov 14 (IANS) Patanjali Foods Limited on Saturday reported a nearly 19 per cent fall in its consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 419.77 crore for the quarter ended September 30 (Q2 FY27), compared to Rs 516.70 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 15.55 per cent year-on-year to Rs 11,322.58 crore, compared to Rs 9,798.84 crore in Q2 FY26. Meanwhile, total income came to Rs 11,406.5 crore against Rs 9,850 crore in the year-ago period. "Q2FY27 performance reflected the resilience of our integrated business model across branded edible oils, upstream oil palm plantations and growing FMCG portfolio,” said Sanjeev Asthana, Chief Executive Officer, Patanjali Foods Limited. Custom Ad: Multiplex He said the quarter also saw a shift in festive demand with Navratri commencing in October this year compared to September last year, while Pitru Paksha during September deferred some festive-led purchases, influencing the timing of festive-led demand and revenue across quarters. Shares of Patanjali Foods ended over 2 per cent lower on Friday at 421 apiece on the BSE. The stock has recorded a 52-week high of Rs 595.20 and a 52-week low of Rs 328.05. In the longer term, the stock remains weak, declining about 6 per cent in six months, 23.93 per cent year-to-date and nearly 30 per cent in one year with underperforming both the Sensex and the BSE FMCG index across all three periods. Over two years, Patanjali Foods shares have fallen over 31 per cent. Earlier in October, the FMCG firm received an order from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in Madhya Pradesh, directing recall of a batch of cow ghee after a sample was found to be unsafe under food safety regulations. MP FDA had issued the order as the sample did not meet standards prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives and Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011, according to the company’s exchange filing. --IANS ag/

articles.title: Strong Domestic Demand, Higher Oil Prices May Push India's FY27 CAD to USD 57 Bn: ICICI Bank
articles.description: Strong Domestic Demand, Higher Oil Prices May Push India's FY27 CAD to USD 57 Bn: ICICI Bank New Delhi, Nov 14 (KNN) India's current account deficit (CAD) is expected to widen to USD 57 billion, or 1.4 per cent of GDP, in FY27 as stronger domestic demand and higher oil prices push up imports despite robust export growth, according to an ICICI Bank report. The bank expects the merchandise trade deficit to reach USD 380 billion, revising its earlier estimate of USD 388 billion, with gold imports likely to remain moderate. “Goods exports have seen a stellar performance in the fiscal year so far (22 per cent YoY), but stronger domestic demand and higher oil prices have driven goods imports higher too (16 per cent YoY),” ANI reported, citing the report. Merchandise Trade Deficit Widens India's merchandise trade deficit widened to nearly USD 40 billion in October, its highest in 12 months, from USD 30.2 billion in September. The increase was driven by an oil deficit of USD 14 billion and a non-oil, non-gold deficit of USD 20 billion. Goods exports rose 45 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to a record USD 49 billion in October, supported by a 140 per cent increase in oil shipments and 33 per cent growth in non-oil exports. However, goods imports increased 17 per cent to a record USD 89 billion, with oil imports rising 54 per cent and non-oil, non-gold imports growing 29 per cent. Services and Capital Flows Support Rupee The bank expects moderate services export growth amid softer demand and disruptions linked to artificial intelligence, while remittances are likely to remain steady. Net services exports rose 13 per cent year-on-year to USD 19.8 billion in October. The recent recovery in foreign portfolio investment (FPI) flows has improved the outlook for the rupee. India received USD 8.8 billion in FPI inflows in November so far, following a period of outflows. ICICI Bank said the improved flows, along with recent RBI measures, made it more constructive on the rupee, although an escalation in the West Asia conflict remained a near-term risk. India's balance of payments remained in surplus during the first half of FY27, supported by strong banking capital inflows, including deposits under the FCNR scheme, the report added. (KNN Bureau)
